newsitem.title: UK: S&P rates Vodohospodarska Vystavba dollar Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates Vodohospodarska Vystavba dollar Eurobond.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it had assigned its BBB minus long-term foreign currency rating to the upcoming US$200 million Eurobond issue by Vodohospodarska Vystavba SP (VV), the state-owned water management company of the Slovak Republic.
"The outlook on the rating is stable," S&P said in a statement.
"The rating is based on the Slovak Republic's unconditional and irrevocable guarantee of the loan agreement to this bond issue, and thus reflects the government's rating," S&P said.
"The stable outlook is based on the continuation of prudent financial policies leading to further inflation reduction and economic growth, as well as increasing export competitiveness."
S&P said VV's business activities included the design and construction of water management projects.
"Additionally, the company participates in engineering planning and design projects including geological engineering research and highway construction," the agency said.
"To date, VV has played a key role in the development of 17 dams, 25 hydro-electric power plants, and 550 kilometres of water and gas pipelines."

"VV has shown an improvement in financial performance in the year ending June 30, with an increase in total revenue of 18 percent from $17.5 million to $20.7 million. This, coupled with the containment of expenditure has lead to an increase in net profits of 69 percent from $854,229 to $1.4 million. Total assets at mid-year 1996 measured $336 million," S&P said.

It said the BBB minus rating of the Slovak Republic was supported by the country's maintenance of prudent economic management, resulting in GDP growth, inflation control, and fiscal and foreign trade performance which ranked among the best of the transition economies.
"The rating is constrained by a still unsettled political situation and some setbacks in the privatization process which have decreased the country's attractiveness to foreign investors," said S&P.
